entities.summary: Titus Annius Luscus (b. 195 BCE, Ancient Rome) was a Roman Senator and military commander of the late Republic era, active in the governance of Roman provinces and the politics of the Roman Senate. He played a significant role in the governance of the Roman province of Cilicia and was involved in the politics of the Roman Senate, contributing to the power struggles of the late Republic. Luscus was known for his military campaigns and his administrative experience, which served him well in his role as a Senator. He was also a patron of the arts and architecture, and his legacy can still be seen in the ruins of ancient Roman cities. Luscus's life and career were marked by his dedication to the Roman Republic and his service to the state, and he remains an important figure in the history of Ancient Rome.
